title: Law and permits
purpose: Nobody films who should not, and no filing is late. Every breach reaches the client and the regulator inside the time limit. Fail any one of these and the contract can end.
how: Compliance is a check at the site, not a folder of papers. Onboarding screening has seven lines, and no phone goes on anyone's head until every line is done. The site nominates the worker and KMSC decides if they are activated. Mano owns the gate, and Mazen and the site's Portfolio Manager run it on launch day. Moharam does not certify a launch until Mano confirms every wearer's file is complete.

The wearer file is our proof, one folder per person. It holds a copy of their ID, the signed consent, the signed fraud briefing, the account in their name, and every wearer log row they appear in. The log ties a flag to a person, not just a phone, and proves the face in the footage gave consent. Mano keeps the file as long as we hold footage of that person.

breaks.what: A worker at the site looks under 18 or has no ID
breaks.do: No phone, whoever assigned them. Tell the Portfolio Manager, who tells Mano the same day. If they already filmed, take the phone that shift. Youssef Medhat holds every session from it. Adham decides what we tell the client.

breaks.what: A wearer asks us to stop, or asks what data we hold about them
breaks.do: Stop filming that person in the same shift. Mano answers with counsel. The Portfolio Manager promises nothing on the spot.

breaks.what: A phone is lost with footage on it
breaks.do: Lost mode within one hour, as the phones and gear page says. From that hour it is a suspected breach. Tell Mano and Moharam, and Adham's 24-hour limit to tell the client starts. If it is not found in 24 hours, wipe it. If we cannot prove it was locked, it is a breach and we send the breach notice.
Mano tells Adham the same day, not a week later. Counsel files it late and tells us what that costs. Put the true new date on the calendar. A missed filing is reported, never hidden.

breaks.what: It is October and a data-protection row is not filed
breaks.do: Adham, Mano, and counsel meet on October 1. They file what is ready, and agree how we film and transfer footage on November 1 if the rest is not filed by then. The date does not move, so the plan changes.

questions.q: Is a video of someone working really personal data?
questions.a: Yes. It shows a face, so it is personal data. That is why we need consent, signage, the licence, and the breach time limits.

questions.q: The site manager says the worker is fine, he just forgot his ID.
questions.a: Then he films tomorrow, with his ID. The site nominates, KMSC activates. No ID, no phone, whoever asks.

questions.q: Who calls the regulator, and who calls the client?
questions.a: Mano calls the regulator, with counsel. Adham calls the client. Nobody else calls either, for any reason.

questions.q: Why is the client's time limit shorter than the regulator's?
questions.a: The contract says 24 hours, and without the contract there is no company. We work to the shorter limit. Meet 24 hours and we meet 72 hours too.

breach.owner: Mano with counsel to the regulator. Adham to the client.
breach.text: A breach is footage or personal data out of our control, including a lost phone we cannot prove was locked. Whoever suspects one tells their Portfolio Manager right away. Moharam and Mano are told within one hour. Adham calls the client within 24 hours. Mano, with counsel, tells the regulator within 72 hours.

gateNote: Onboarding screening is the compliance check at the site: seven lines, and no phone goes on anyone until every line is done. The lines are on the onboarding page. This page explains what is behind them.
